method: blind: two builds as X and Y, reviewer not told which was which. X = now (client 51091980, cross-frame attention on); Y = M111 final (client d2d27404, server --engine-arg xframe=0). Walking filmstrips, 8 frames 0.15 s apart at 3.4 m/s, all 8 zones (tools/shoot.mjs --strip).
reviewer: a fresh-context Claude Opus 5.5 session with no other context
notes: part of the new build's steadiness comes from painting less in places (haze in the nave, a blank slab in the desert, bare walls in the baths)
sharpness is even on average (2.8 each): the new build is sharper in 3 zones by larger margins, the old in 5
both builds show ghost geometry: tilted translucent rectangles in the vestibule, thin pane lines in the nave, a ghost-building rectangle in the desert sky
new build only: an unpainted wall strip in the geode (first frame), a blueprint border and ghost lettering in the atrium, dotted tick lines in the garden, a flat brown slab in the desert
summary: I'd rather walk through X [now]. It holds its world together in 7 of 8 zones, and even its weakest zone is a readable corridor. Y [M111] keeps reinventing the things you look at (the garden shrine, the geode crystals, the end wall of the nave), and its atrium can't be read at all.
prompt_summary: per zone: which build keeps things the same from frame to frame, which is sharper, artifacts, 1-5 grades for steadiness and sharpness, overall preference; judge only the pictures
